Improving bulk purchases with a redesigned quantity modal

Most retailers were buying the smallest quantity and missing out on better bulk prices. I redesigned the quantity modal so those savings are clear and easy to act on.

  • RoleProduct designer
  • CompanyBadho
  • TeamPM lead, APM, dev
  • ShippedJul 2025

The results

2 months before vs 2 months after launch

  • Avg order value
    +20%Bigger baskets per order
  • Rejected orders
    −12%Fewer orders turned down
  • Spend per buyer
    +4.1%More spent per retailer
  • Total orders
    +7.5%More orders placed

Two apps, one marketplace

Badho is a B2B e-commerce platform where kirana (neighbourhood grocery) store owners buy stock directly from FMCG distributors. It runs on two apps, and this project lives in the buyer app.

Buyer appRetailers place ordersThis project
Seller appDistributors fulfil them

Problem Statement

Many products on Badho have slab pricing: the more you buy, the lower the price per piece. The quantity modal is where retailers decide how much to buy, so it's the natural place to show these bulk deals.

Iterations I tried

I explored three versions, and each one built on what worked in the one before.

V1

What could be better

✕Cognitive load: too much info
✕Poor accessibility, too little spacing within CTAs
✕Design lacks motivation to buy in bulk

What worked well

✓Policies kept for each slab
✓Grouping: product info and qty-price info sit together
✓All pricing slabs upfront, in a familiar vertical scroll

V2

What could be better

✕Grouping: qty and amount are kept apart
✕Removed slab policies
✕Design lacks motivation to buy in bulk

What worked well

✓Motivation through offers and a purchase-qty progress bar
✓Lower cognitive load than V1

V3, final

What could be better

✕Removed slab policies, so they need to show at other entry points
✕Slabs in a horizontal scroll; as qty updates we auto-select the slab and move the margin bar

What worked well

✓Motivation through offers and purchase-qty progress
✓Lower cognitive load than V1 and V2
✓Consistent with the app design language
✓Intuitive interactions and sound

Before and after

Margin progress bar with slabs, so you always see which margin slab you're in
Bigger, clearer slab cards with direct action buttons
New keypad with a shorter height and slab-add suggestions built in
Pricing slabs had little hierarchy and small fonts
Primary focus went to seller policies
The number keypad took up more space, squeezing out slab info

Looking back

🤖Used AI as a thinking partner

To explore ideas, validate directions and iterate faster. It led to solutions like the progress indicator.

🤝Stakeholder management is key

Aligning stakeholders on what truly mattered sharpened visual priority and put focus on the key decision-making elements.

👥Collaborated closely with cross-functional teams

Continuous feedback helped refine and successfully deliver the final design.

🎁Future scope for free gifts and other incentives

Today it focuses on quantity-based discounts. Next, the modal should clearly show every bulk benefit, like free items.

🔎Conduct deeper user research

To better understand how retailers decide on bulk purchases, and optimize how incentives are presented.

📊Continue iterating on metrics and feedback

Keep improving clarity and usability based on product metrics and real user behaviour.
